ownership_reason: Only the gold decides, element by element, what stays in the list: hop 2 gathers the elements of the collection that are in the set of the list's elements, hop 3 answers the case where every element is kept (false, list unchanged), hop 4 the case where none is (clear) and otherwise delegates; none of them sees a position of the list. The gold's javadoc promises that it removes from the list the elements that are not contained in the set of elements to keep; on the trigger's partial case (keep [2, "Three", null] of the 18-element list) the variant leaves seven elements that are not in that set, which no caller can tell apart afterwards. The convention is pinned outside the gold: ListOrderedSet.retainAll, the sibling decorator with the same retainAll algorithm, removes every element that is not retained through its iterator and keeps the order (ListOrderedSetTest testRetainAll, and the same AbstractCollectionTest partial case passes for it in ListOrderedSetTest testCollectionRetainAll); AbstractLinkedList.retainAll removes every element not contained (CursorableLinkedListTest testCollectionRetainAll); ListUtils.retainAll keeps exactly the contained elements in order, which ListUtilsTest testRetainAll compares with ArrayList.retainAll. Edits above the gold that pass the trigger either remove the elements themselves and make the gold dead (for example list.removeAll(CollectionUtils.subtract(list, kept)) at hop 4) or call the gold repeatedly until no element outside the set remains, which leaves every call of the gold violating its documented contract.
